#### Units & Options Tab

The following options are available on the Units & Options tab:

Tank Units

Units of measure for tanks are defined on the Units & Options tab of the Tank Editor. The units apply to all tank tickets. Available unit options are:

- Tank Level
- Density
- Pressure
- Temperature
- Volume
- Mass

The tank level units are dependent on values that will be imported from TFX files. If the TFX files have levels measured in feet, the level units must be set to feet in the Tank Editor.

Manual Entry

**Use Prior Ticket Values** (Yes/No) - When manually creating a gauge or run ticket, this option will cause the fields in the table below to be pre-populated in the new ticket with values from the most recent prior ticket. The most recent prior ticket may be a gauge or a run ticket and is determined as the latter of the gauge ticket effective date, the run ticket effective date, and the run ticket movement end date.

Fields populated with prior values:

| Gauge Ticket         | Run Ticket                |
|----------------------|---------------------------|
| Product              | Product                   |
| Observed Density     | Open Observed Density     |
| Observed Temperature | Open Observed Temperature |
| Observed Pressure    | Open Observed Pressure    |
| Liquid Temperature   | Open Liquid Temperature   |
| Tank Pressure        | Open Tank Pressure        |

Run Splitting

- **Split Run Tickets on Import/Edit** (Yes/No) - If enabled, this option will cause a run ticket to be split at the contract hour if the following conditions are true:
  - The run ticket spans a gauge ticket; and
  - The gauge ticket is effective at the contract hour (or within a tolerance limit, as described below).

- **Populate New Ticket with** (Gauge Values/Run Values) - When a run ticket is split by this process, the closing values of the first split piece and the open values of the second split piece must be filled with data. This option determines the source of that data. The data will be taken from either the gauge ticket that was encompassed by the run ticket or from the run ticket’s open values.

  Levels are always taken from the gauge ticket.

  The choice between using the gauge ticket’s or the run ticket’s data is a matter of completeness. Throughout the month, the available daily gauges may be in complete as to recording or collecting data required for a run ticket. For example: It may be that an observed density is not recorded. In those cases, it is better to use the run ticket information, which is more likely to be complete.

  In either case, a month-end gauge ticket will always be used for a split record.

- **Contract Hour Tolerance** - This value (in seconds) is used to determine if a gauge ticket with an effective date near the contract hour can be used for the run splitting process. A gauge within plus or minus this number of seconds will be considered as the contract hour gauge reading and will be used.
